inputs.original_text: PARIS, France— In a case that has sent ripples of concern through religious communities and civil liberties advocates across France, a French abbot has been convicted under a controversial new law targeting “psychological subjection.” The conviction of Father Bernard Domini, superior of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame (FMND), under France’s new law has ignited a [...]
inputs.modified_text: France’s conviction of Father Bernard Domini under the new law on “psychological subjection” highlights the power imbalance that can leave people vulnerable to coercive authority. Religious freedom should protect belief, not give powerful institutions immunity from accountability. The state must not control conscience either: protections need clear, fair standards and safeguards against unchecked official power. The focus should be on whether people are being harmed, and on holding institutions accountable without targeting faith itself.
